title: 2. What the Company Does: Segments, Revenue Mix & Concrete Examples
summary: A granular breakdown of Intuitive Surgical's three revenue pillars—Instruments & Accessories ($6.02B, 59.8% of FY2025 revenue), Systems ($2.47B, 24.5%), and Services ($1.57B, 15.6%)—alongside procedure mix, US/OUS geography, and end-to-end real-world hospital economics.

epigraph.quote: The system placement is merely the handshake; the economic relationship begins when the sterile instrument tray opens for case number one.
epigraph.author: Hospital Supply Chain Economics

web_blocks.html: 2.1 Revenue Architecture: The Three-Legged Razor-and-Blade Engine

Intuitive Surgical reports revenue in three linked lines: Instruments and Accessories (I&A), Systems, and Services [1, 2]. Headlines focus on quarterly robot placements, but recurring case volume drives the business. In FY2025, total sales hit $10,064.7 million (+20.5% YoY) [1, 5]. I&A brought in $6,020 million (59.8%), Systems $2,470 million (24.5%), and Services $1,570 million (15.6%) [1, 5]. Through 9M 2026, total sales rose 21.0% YoY to $8,711.8 million, split across I&A ($5,218.7 million, 59.9%), Systems ($2,104.8 million, 24.2%), and Services ($1,388.3 million, 15.9%) [3]. Counting lease revenue inside Systems and Service contracts, recurring sales hit $2.55 billion in Q3 2026 alone—about 84% of total revenue [4].

web_blocks.caption: Intuitive Surgical Revenue Mix: FY2024, FY2025, and 9M 2026 ($ Millions)
web_blocks.takeaway: I&A and Services together represent 75.4% of FY2025 revenue and 75.8% of 9M 2026 revenue; adding operating-lease payments inside Systems lifts total recurring revenue to ~84%.

web_blocks.html: The United States remains Intuitive's core profit pool, generating 68% of FY2025 revenue (up from 67% in 2024 and 66% in 2023) [1]. Outside of the United States (OUS) markets supplied the remaining 32% [1]. Higher U.S. procedure intensity per robot and the early U.S. da Vinci 5 ramp drive that domestic share [1, 5]. Still, international case volume is growing faster: OUS da Vinci cases grew 23% in FY2025 versus 18% globally [5]. European general surgery, Japanese and Korean cancer care, and hospital networks in India and China led that OUS growth [1, 15].

General Surgery—hernia repair, gallbladder removal, colon resection, and bariatric care—is Intuitive's largest and fastest-growing specialty worldwide [1, 2]. In hernia repair, robotic precision cuts recurrence and chronic pain; in colon cancer, wristed tips aid tight pelvic work [1, 2]. Gynecology (hysterectomy, myomectomy, endometriosis) ranks second in the U.S., while Urology (prostate and kidney cancer) serves as a steady domestic base and strong OUS anchor [1, 2]. Thoracic lung surgery and throat cancer cases add high-acuity mix. Meanwhile, Ion Endoluminal bronchoscopy is Intuitive's fastest-growing standalone engine (+51% in FY2025 and +31% in Q3 2026) [4, 5]. Complex cancer and colon cases also use robotic staplers, vessel sealers, and more EndoWrist tools, lifting I&A revenue per case above simpler benign surgeries [1, 2].
2.3 Concrete End-to-End Real-World Examples by Segment

Segment 1 — Instruments & Accessories (Concrete Example: Community Hospital Hernia & Colorectal Program): Picture a 400-bed U.S. regional hospital doing 1,200 da Vinci general surgery cases a year on three systems. For a ventral hernia or low colon resection, open surgery brings higher infection risk and longer stays, while rigid sticks make internal suturing tiring. Before each case, sterile-processing staff pull a custom kit of EndoWrist tools (Maryland bipolar forceps, curved scissors, needle driver, SureForm staplers), sterile drapes, seals, and energy cartridges [1, 2]. Each reusable EndoWrist tool carries an encrypted RFID chip that limits it to a set number of uses—usually 10 to 18 lives—before the console locks it out to protect cable safety [1, 20]. Shipped weekly from Mexicali and Sunnyvale hubs, these tools and disposables generate roughly $1,800 to $2,400+ in I&A sales per da Vinci case [1, 5]. Every surgery turns into predictable, high-margin consumption [1, 5].

Segment 2 — Systems (Concrete Example: Multi-Hospital IDN Upgrading to da Vinci 5 & Ion): Consider a large Integrated Delivery Network (IDN) replacing older Si/Xi robots and adding lung diagnostics. An outright da Vinci purchase costs $0.6 million to $3.1 million based on configuration, with da Vinci 5 near the top and Ion around $450,000–$500,000 [1, 21]. Because hospital CFOs face tight capital budgets, Intuitive offers cash sales, sales-type leases, and fixed or usage-based operating leases [1, 2]. In FY2025, 872 of 1,721 global da Vinci placements (50.7%) used operating leases, including 496 usage-based deals where hospitals pay per case [5]. Once signed, Intuitive field engineers install the patient cart, surgeon console, and vision tower, align the 3D optics, and link the unit to hospital IT for software updates [9]. In the pulmonology suite, an Ion tower (~$450K–$500K) consumes single-use 3.5 mm catheters (~$4,000–$4,500 benchmark), guides (~$1,500), and Flexision biopsy needles on every case [10, 21].

Segment 3 — Services (Concrete Example: 24/7 Uptime Guarantee & Digital Telemetry): An academic hospital running 450 robotic cases per robot each year cannot afford an unscheduled room shutdown. Idle nursing, anesthesia, and surgeon time costs thousands of dollars per hour. Every da Vinci and Ion unit carries a multi-year service plan, bundled in year one and renewed yearly at roughly $100,000–$200,000+ per system [1]. Intuitive field engineers run preventive checks, swap worn German-built endoscopes, and track live machine health through the MyIntuitive cloud portal [9]. With September 2025 FDA clearance of Network CCM remote updates and Video Replay on da Vinci 5, Services now includes case analytics and surgeon dashboards [1, 9]. That software layer turns a basic hardware warranty into a sticky clinical operating system [1, 9].

Together, the three segments act as a self-reinforcing flywheel rather than separate lines [1, 2]. High service uptime keeps daily OR schedules full; full schedules drive EndoWrist and Ion catheter use; rising tool use gives hospital leaders the ROI to add robots via leases or da Vinci 5 upgrades [4, 5]. In addition, I&A and Services carry much higher gross margins than new hardware [1, 5]. So total gross profit dollars compound steadily even in quarters when usage-based leases defer upfront Systems revenue [1, 5].

One key accounting rule separates outright sales and sales-type leases from operating leases [1, 2]. Under an outright sale or sales-type lease, Intuitive books the full $0.6M–$3.1M value in Systems revenue at installation. Under a fixed or usage-based operating lease (50.7% of 2025 placements), Intuitive keeps the robot on its balance sheet as a depreciating asset and books payments over the 5–7 year term [1, 5]. Operating leases defer near-term Systems revenue, but they usually earn more total lifetime cash per robot and shield demand from hospital capital freezes [1, 5].

web_blocks.title: Why Operating Leases Expand the Addressable Base Without Destroying Economics
paragraphs: Placing a da Vinci 5 on a usage-based operating lease defers upfront Systems revenue in exchange for higher per-case cash flow over 5–7 years [1, 5]. Hospitals skip capital-committee delays, while Intuitive locks in long-term I&A and Service annuities.

book_subsections.title: The Three-Legged Razor-and-Blade Engine
paragraphs: If you look at Intuitive Surgical from the outside, it is easy to mistake it for a heavy capital-equipment manufacturer—a company that builds expensive robots and sells them one by one to hospitals. Nothing could be further from the financial truth. In fiscal 2025, Intuitive generated $10.06 billion in total revenue, and nearly 60 percent of that—$6.02 billion—came not from selling robots, but from selling the instruments and accessories consumed inside every operation. Add $1.57 billion in annual service contracts, plus the recurring operating-lease payments embedded inside the $2.47 billion Systems line, and you discover that roughly 84 percent of Intuitive's quarterly revenue in Q3 2026 was recurring.

That recurring share is the secret behind Intuitive's compounding resilience. Two-thirds of the company's revenue comes from the United States, where procedure intensity per robot is highest, while the remaining third comes from international markets in Europe, Japan, Korea, China, and India—regions that are growing procedures even faster than the domestic base as general surgery and oncology adopt minimally invasive robotics.

book_subsections.title: Walking Inside the Hospital: How Each Dollar Actually Flows
paragraphs: To make these three segments concrete, let us walk inside a 400-bed regional hospital in the Midwest that operates three da Vinci systems. Suppose a general surgeon schedules a complex ventral hernia repair or a colorectal cancer resection. In the sterile-processing room down the hall, technicians pull a tray of EndoWrist instruments—bipolar forceps, monopolar scissors, needle drivers, and robotic staplers—alongside sterile drapes and seals. Every EndoWrist instrument carries an encrypted memory chip that counts its clinical uses, typically 10 to 18 procedures depending on the tool, before the console locks it out so worn cables never snap inside a patient. After the operation, those instruments are washed and autoclaved, and once their counter hits zero, the hospital orders replacements from Intuitive's distribution hubs. That single case generates roughly two thousand dollars of recurring Instruments and Accessories revenue.

Now look at the Systems segment. When that same hospital system wants to add a new da Vinci 5—which carries an outright price tag at the upper end of Intuitive's $0.6 million to $3.1 million system band—or an Ion robotic bronchoscopy tower priced near $450,000 to $500,000, the hospital CFO often balks at writing a multi-million-dollar capital check. Intuitive solves that friction with flexible financing. In 2025, more than half of all da Vinci placements—872 out of 1,721 systems—went out under operating leases, including 496 usage-based leases where the hospital pays per procedure performed. Meanwhile, in the pulmonology suite, every Ion lung biopsy consumes a single-use 3.5-millimeter shape-sensing catheter and biopsy needle, replicating the exact same razor-and-blade economics outside the abdomen.

Finally, look at Services. An idle operating room costs a hospital thousands of dollars an hour. Intuitive's annual maintenance contracts—generating $1.57 billion in 2025—pay for field engineers, German-built endoscope replacements, and 24/7 remote telemetry. With the 2025 FDA clearance of Network CCM remote updates and In-Console Video Replay on da Vinci 5, that service contract now delivers cloud-based surgical analytics and case review directly inside the surgeon's viewer.

Pause for a moment to appreciate how all three segments reinforce one another inside that hospital. The Services team keeps the da Vinci and Ion towers running at near-100 percent uptime, which maximizes daily case throughput; higher case throughput drives higher consumption of encrypted EndoWrist instruments and Ion catheters; and higher instrument volume convinces the hospital's surgical committee to add a fourth or fifth da Vinci 5 system under a usage-based lease. That closed loop—hardware reliability feeding procedure volume, which feeds recurring consumables, which justifies fleet expansion—is why Intuitive's revenue base has compounded across every medical-budget cycle for two decades.

Let us also trace the geographic and specialty nuance that underpins those numbers, because not every procedure or region carries identical economics. In the United States—which generated 68 percent of Intuitive's $10.06 billion revenue in 2025—general surgery is the dominant growth engine. Think of inguinal hernias, ventral hernias, gallbladders, and colorectal cancer resections: these are high-frequency procedures performed in virtually every community hospital and outpatient surgery center. When a surgeon moves from open or straight-stick laparoscopic hernia repair to da Vinci, the hospital consumes basic EndoWrist scissors, graspers, and needle drivers; when that same surgeon performs a complex colorectal resection or thoracic lobectomy, the tray expands to include robotic SureForm staplers and advanced vessel sealers, lifting per-procedure instrument revenue.

Outside the United States—32 percent of revenue in 2025, but growing procedures at 23 percent compared with 18 percent globally—the adoption curve looks different. In Europe, Japan, South Korea, and emerging hubs like India, robotic surgery often anchors first in high-acuity cancer centers (urology, thoracic, and colorectal oncology) before broadening into benign general surgery as reimbursement codes mature. Meanwhile, Ion endoluminal bronchoscopy is building a parallel recurring engine in pulmonary medicine: with 1,152 Ion systems installed globally by September 2026 and procedure volume growing 31 percent in Q3 2026, each peripheral lung biopsy consumes a single-use 3.5-millimeter shape-sensing catheter, guide, and biopsy needle—turning lung-cancer diagnosis into an annuity that sits completely outside the abdominal OR.

book_subsections.title: Why Lease Accounting Masks True Economic Demand
paragraphs: One subtlety you and I must always keep straight when reading Intuitive's quarterly income statement is the accounting difference between an outright sale, a sales-type lease, and an operating lease. When a hospital pays cash upfront or signs a sales-type lease, Intuitive recognizes the full $0.6 million to $3.1 million system price immediately in Systems revenue. When that same hospital chooses a fixed-payment or usage-based operating lease—as happened on 872 of the 1,721 da Vinci placements in 2025—Intuitive retains the robot on its own balance sheet as a depreciating asset and recognizes lease revenue gradually over the five-to-seven-year contract as procedures are performed.

In the short run, a higher operating-lease mix depresses reported Systems revenue and ties up working capital. Over the full life of the robot, however, usage-based leases typically generate higher cumulative revenue and cash flow than an outright cash sale, while dramatically lowering the barrier for community hospitals and Ambulatory Surgery Centers to adopt da Vinci 5 or Ion. Whenever you see Systems revenue fluctuate from quarter to quarter, check the placement count and operating-lease share first—because the underlying clinical demand is almost always steadier than the GAAP top line makes it appear.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: The Quiet Power of Usage-Based Leases
book_callouts.text: Notice how Intuitive Surgical turns hospital capital scarcity into a competitive weapon. By placing nearly half of its new systems on operating leases—and nearly 500 a year on usage-based leases—management removes the CFO's upfront capex veto while locking in years of high-margin instrument and service cash flows.
